properties.title: German Third Army: northern operational axis
properties.note: The documented northern pincer advanced from East Prussia toward the Narew and the area east of Warsaw. This arrow shows the broad direction, not a unit route or its position on either selected day.
properties.uncertainty: Waypoints are cartographic guides, not surveyed troop positions.

properties.title: German Fourth Army: Pomeranian Corridor axis
properties.note: Fourth Army attacked from Pomerania to cut the Polish Corridor and link with forces from East Prussia. The arrow indicates the documented strategic direction only.
properties.uncertainty: No exact route or date-specific unit position is asserted.

properties.title: German Tenth Army: southern pincer axis
properties.note: Tenth Army was assigned the main thrust from Silesia toward Warsaw. This arrow depicts the planned and executed broad axis, not a continuous unit track.
properties.uncertainty: Endpoints indicate direction, not occupied ground on the selected date.

properties.title: German Fourteenth Army: southern approach
properties.note: Fourteenth Army attacked from the southern approaches, including Slovakia, toward Polish territory. This is a generalized direction, not a verified road or troop route.
properties.uncertainty: The line is schematic and must not be read as a daily front.

properties.title: Soviet Byelorussian Front: western advance
properties.note: The Byelorussian Front attacked into northeastern Poland from the Soviet border. This arrow shows a broad westward direction, not a formation's route or the ground held on 17 September.
properties.uncertainty: The arrow is directional only; individual army routes remain unmapped.

properties.title: Soviet Ukrainian Front: western advance
properties.note: The Ukrainian Front attacked eastern Poland from the Soviet border. This arrow shows the broad direction toward eastern Galicia, not a detailed unit route or a 17 September front line.
properties.uncertainty: The arrow is directional only; local positions remain unmapped.
